_meta.description: Cinematic definitions (standards 3.2). Data-driven: camera paths in site-scene metres (x east from AOI west edge, z south from AOI north edge, y elevation), target point (or path), duration, easing, purpose tag, captions, and a text description (audio-description script). Every shot is skippable from the first frame and has a reduced-motion still version. Total duration 60 s <= 90 s budget. None plays during an assessment.

captions: Coming down over the Apennine Front — mountains thrust up when a giant impact reshaped the Moon 3.9 billion years ago.
Below, the mare plain. The winding line is Hadley Rille. The pin is your landing site, between the mountain and the channel — exactly where Apollo 15 landed in 1971.
shots.description: The camera starts high above the southern mountains at low sun and descends northward across the mountain front to the flat plain, ending above the landing-site marker.

captionsPerStill: High over the Apennine Front at low Sun.
Crossing the mountain front; the rille appears on the plain.
The landing-site marker between the rille and the mountains.

captions: The Sun sinks toward the horizon. Watch the rille and the crater rims appear from the shadows.
This is why the crew landed just after local sunrise: at a low Sun angle, relief is unmistakable.
shots.description: A fixed view toward the rille while the sunlight sweeps from high noon to near sunrise; long shadows crawl across the plain and the channel deepens into contrast.

captionsPerStill: High Sun: the plain looks flat.
Low Sun: the rille and crater rims stand out in shadow.

captions: Your job is to finish their survey: read the land, compare the crater records, plan a traverse.
In 1971 Scott and Irwin drove 27 kilometres in three days. Where will YOU go?
shots.description: The camera rises and pulls back as a map overlay fades in showing the real Apollo 15 traverse routes beside the landing site.

captionsPerStill: The site from above, with the real Apollo 15 traverse marked.
